facts.big: The book was written by a doctor
facts.label: Passivo no passado com by
facts.sub: Use was/were + participle: The book was written by a doctor. The film was directed by a young man. Use by para dizer quem fez.

facts.label: Was/were + particípio
facts.sub: Use was/were + particípio para falar de livros, filmes e coisas feitas: The book was published ten years ago. The books were sold in many countries.

facts.label: Por quem
facts.sub: Depois do passivo, by diz quem fez: written by a doctor, directed by a young man, designed by her daughter. Sem o agente, a frase também funciona: It was published ten years ago.

compare.ask: It was written by a doctor.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “foi escrito por” e “foi dirigido por”.
compare.tip: Diga: “It was written by a doctor.”
compare.us: Em inglês, usamos was/were + particípio + by: The book was written by a doctor. The film was directed by a young man.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: It was written by a doctor.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We say “was written by” for books.
We say “was directed by” for films.
We say “The book wrote by a doctor.”
items.why: We say The book was written by a doctor.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We say “was written by” for books. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “was directed by” for films. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “The book wrote by a doctor.” → Falso (We say The book was written by a doctor.)

paragraphs: It is a quiet afternoon in Denver. Carlos goes to his friend Hal’s bookshop. The author of one book is a doctor. There is a shelf full of paperback books. Hal puts a bookmark on his favorite page. Carlos wants a gift for his sister.

“Carlos, look at this book. It was written by a doctor from Denver.” says Hal. “Really? Was it published this year?” says Carlos. “No, it was published ten years ago. The cover was designed by her daughter.” says Hal.
